exports.n: rank 5: exports (1.87 Mt) are above its smelter output in the USGS table (1.10 Mt). HS 7601 includes alloy ingot, which can be made from scrap, and Malaysia receives 0.54 Mt from the United States (a possible reading, not established here)

Customs data record 1.1 Mt of iron ore from Malaysia to Switzerland in 2024 (7.7% of Malaysia's recorded exports and 94.9% of Switzerland's recorded imports, CEPII BACI). Switzerland has no coast and is a trading centre for commodities, so the cargo probably ends elsewhere and the customs record only the declared country: a possible reading, not established here. The tonnes stay in the tables and are counted at the passages of the route to its declared destination; no generated route is built from this pair; Malaysia is both an importer (rank 4, 25.7 Mt) and an exporter (rank 11, 14.4 Mt) of iron ore: ore may be transshipped, stored or blended there and shipped on, which counts the same ore in two countries' trade (a possible reading, not established here)

imports.n: Unwrought aluminium (HS 7601) from the United States to Malaysia: 0.536 Mt in 2024 (CEPII BACI), declared at 1,034 USD per tonne, 40% of the tonne-weighted median of the group (2,565); the 2024 average aluminium price is 2,419 USD per tonne (World Bank Pink Sheet), and the pair is declared at 43% of it. Material priced like scrap or alloy, or another cheaper product, declared under this code is a plausible cause; it is not established here.
